ask-verb-1acc9c10.why: 'Interrogar' means to interrogate formally, which does not match everyday 'ask' and contradicts note[1].

box-noun-fb138ba4.fix: Cuadrado o espacio pequeño en una página o pantalla donde se escribe o se marca una opción. | casilla, recuadro
box-noun-fb138ba4.why: Everyday A2 meaning ('check the box', 'write in the box') is missing.
'Caseta' is not in any of the entry's senses.

box-noun-fb138ba4.quote: La palabra 'box' se refiere principalmente a una caja con lados planos, pero también puede

busy-adj-c3c2275e.quote: Un lugar donde hay mucha gente o mucha actividad.
busy-adj-c3c2275e.fix: Dicho de un lugar, que tiene mucha gente, tráfico o actividad.
busy-adj-c3c2275e.why: Defines a noun ('un lugar') instead of an adjective.

busy-adj-c3c2275e.quote: Usa 'busy' para describir a una persona que tiene mucho trabajo o una agenda llena.
busy-adj-c3c2275e.fix: Para indicar en qué se está ocupado, se usa directamente el verbo en '-ing' o 'with' + sustantivo (por ejemplo, 'busy cooking' o 'busy with work'), no 'in'.
busy-adj-c3c2275e.why: Merely repeats the definition of sense 0 without adding usage guidance.

call-verb-724aa94d.quote: Por favor llama su nombre para que nos escuche.
call-verb-724aa94d.fix: Por favor, grita su nombre para que nos escuche.
call-verb-724aa94d.why: 'Llamar su nombre' is an unnatural calque in Spanish; use 'gritar/decir su nombre' or 'llamarla'.

call-verb-724aa94d.quote: Se usa tanto para el contacto telefónico como para gritar el nombre de alguien desde
call-verb-724aa94d.fix: A diferencia del español ('llamar a alguien'), 'call' no lleva preposición antes de la persona: se dice 'call your mother', no 'call to your mother'.
call-verb-724aa94d.why: Only restates the meanings already given in senses 0 and 1.

door-noun-39cd983e.quote: Se usa para la entrada física de una casa o habitación, pero también de forma
door-noun-39cd983e.fix: Para decir que alguien está llamando o esperando en la puerta, se usa la preposición 'at' ('Someone is at the door').
door-noun-39cd983e.why: Restates the literal sense and mentions a figurative sense absent from the entry.

hair-noun-ebe4b0af.fix: Para referirse al conjunto del pelo, 'hair' es incontable y se usa siempre en singular ('Her hair is long'). Solo es contable ('a hair', 'hairs') para hablar de pelos individuales.
hair-noun-ebe4b0af.why: Learners need to know 'hair' is uncountable when referring to hair as a mass.

juice-noun-ba520c0a.quote: En Estados Unidos se utiliza principalmente la palabra 'juice' para referirse a cualquier bebida
juice-noun-ba520c0a.fix: En español, 'juice' se traduce como 'jugo' en América Latina y como 'zumo' en España.
juice-noun-ba520c0a.why: Restates the definition of 'juice' and confuses English 'juice' with Spanish 'jugo' versus 'zumo'.

juice-noun-ba520c0a.quote: La palabra 'juice' también puede usarse de forma figurada para hablar de la energía
juice-noun-ba520c0a.why: Merely repeats the meaning already given in sense 1.

laugh-verb-67b08ddd.why: 'carcajada' is a noun gloss and is not among the verb senses.

laugh-verb-67b08ddd.quote: Aunque 'laugh' puede ser tanto un verbo como un sustantivo, su uso principal es
laugh-verb-67b08ddd.fix: Para indicar de qué o de quién se ríe alguien, se usa con la preposición 'at' ('laugh at someone/something').
laugh-verb-67b08ddd.why: Saying its main use is to describe the action of laughing merely restates the gloss.

das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.quote: The upper interior surface of a space, like a car interior or a tunnel.
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.why: 'Dach' is an exterior roof (including a car's roof); an interior ceiling is 'die Decke'.
'top' is not among the glosses; 'Dach' means 'roof'.

das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.quote: While 'Dach' most commonly refers to the structural roof of a building, it is
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.fix: The plural is 'die Dächer'. Do not confuse 'das Dach' (the roof on top of a building or car) with 'die Decke' (the ceiling inside a room).
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.why: A car's 'Dach' is its exterior roof, not a ceiling; also misses plural 'Dächer'.

stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.fix: To ask a question or make a formal request. | to ask, to pose, to make
stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.why: Missing the common A1/A2 sense in collocations like 'eine Frage stellen' (to ask a question).

stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.quote: Use stellen when placing something in a vertical or standing position (like a chair,
stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.why: Restates sense 0's definition and duplicates the explanation in note 1.

stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.fix: 'Stellen' expresses movement into a standing position and takes the accusative with two-way prepositions ('auf den Tisch'), unlike 'stehen' (location, dative: 'auf dem Tisch').
stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.why: Learners need the contrast with 'stehen' (to stand) and the accusative with two-way prepositions.

letter-noun-ea13e543.quote: La palabra 'letter' tiene dos significados muy comunes: un mensaje escrito (carta) y un
letter-noun-ea13e543.fix: En español 'letra' también se usa para canciones ('lyrics') y caligrafía ('handwriting'), pero en inglés no.
letter-noun-ea13e543.why: Restates the two senses and glosses already shown in the entry.

letter-noun-ea13e543.quote: La palabra gato empieza con la letra c.
letter-noun-ea13e543.fix: La palabra «cat» empieza con la letra c.
letter-noun-ea13e543.why: Translating 'cat' as 'gato' makes the statement about starting with 'c' false.

line-noun-f3348969.quote: Serie de personas o cosas colocadas una detrás de otra mientras esperan su turno.
line-noun-f3348969.fix: Serie de personas o cosas colocadas una detrás de otra.
line-noun-f3348969.why: Inanimate things in a line do not wait their turn.

line-noun-f3348969.fix: Ruta o servicio de transporte público, o conexión telefónica. | línea
line-noun-f3348969.why: Missing the common everyday sense of a transit route or phone line.

line-noun-f3348969.quote: Para una marca dibujada o una línea geométrica, también se usa 'line'.
line-noun-f3348969.why: Merely restates the second sense without adding usage information.

museum-noun-13e50ed9.quote: A diferencia del español, donde se dice 'museo' con acento en la última sílaba,
museum-noun-13e50ed9.fix: En inglés la primera sílaba se pronuncia /mju/ y el acento recae en la segunda: /mjuˈziːəm/.
museum-noun-13e50ed9.why: Spanish 'museo' (mu-se-o) is stressed on the second syllable, not the last.

name-noun-a25a0089.why: 'Apellido' is not a sense of 'name' alone, and sense 1 is omitted.

name-noun-a25a0089.quote: Se usa para referirse al nombre de pila de una persona, así como a
name-noun-a25a0089.fix: Para especificar el nombre de pila se usa 'first name', y para el apellido, 'last name' o 'surname'.
name-noun-a25a0089.why: Alone, 'name' means full or given name; 'last name' is needed for surname.

name-noun-a25a0089.quote: Palabra o conjunto de palabras con que se designa a una persona.
name-noun-a25a0089.fix: Palabra o conjunto de palabras con que se designa a una persona, animal, lugar o cosa.
name-noun-a25a0089.why: Too narrow; 'name' applies to places, things, and animals, not just people.

name-noun-a25a0089.label: proper-name
name-noun-a25a0089.fix: Please write your full name at the top of the page.
name-noun-a25a0089.why: Examples must not contain personal names.

name-noun-a25a0089.label: proper-name
name-noun-a25a0089.fix: Por favor, escribe tu nombre completo en la parte superior de la página.
name-noun-a25a0089.why: Matches the corrected example without a personal name.

train-noun-a4d69b7d.quote: Aunque 'train' se traduce principalmente como 'tren', también puede usarse para describir una serie
train-noun-a4d69b7d.fix: Para indicar el medio de transporte se dice 'by train' («en tren», sin artículo), y para ubicarse en él o subir y bajar se usa 'on' ('on the train', 'get on/off the train'), no 'in'.
train-noun-a4d69b7d.why: Restates the senses and mentions a wedding-dress sense not in the definitions.

el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.quote: The way a person is dressed; clothing or attire in general.
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.why: As 'clothing in general', 'vestido' is formal and restricted; beginners need 'ropa'.

el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.quote: El código de vestido para el evento es formal.
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.fix: El código de vestimenta para el evento es formal.
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.why: 'Código de vestido' is a false calque of 'dress code'; Spanish uses 'código de vestimenta'.

la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.label: example.proper-noun
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.quote: Mi familia vive en un pueblo pequeño cerca de Madrid.
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.fix: Mi familia vive en un pueblo pequeño cerca de la costa.
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.why: Examples must not contain names of places.

a-veces-adv-566ce858.quote: Used to express that an action happens occasionally but not always.
a-veces-adv-566ce858.why: Merely restates the definition and glosses without adding usage information.

amar-verb-953e673e.quote: To like someone or something very much.
amar-verb-953e673e.fix: To feel a deep passion or fondness for something. | love, adore
amar-verb-953e673e.why: Amar expresses deep love or passion, not 'liking someone very much' (contradicts note[0]).

amar-verb-953e673e.quote: Ella dice que ama bailar los fines de semana.
amar-verb-953e673e.fix: Ella ama la música y el arte.
amar-verb-953e673e.why: In Castilian Spanish, 'encantar' is used with infinitives for hobbies; 'amar' takes a noun.

amar-verb-953e673e.quote: to love; to like very much
amar-verb-953e673e.why: Amar does not mean 'to like very much'.

dar-verb-7cb7de0d.fix: To cause a feeling or perform an action expressed by a noun. | give, cause, take
dar-verb-7cb7de0d.why: Lacks the common light-verb sense (e.g. dar miedo, dar un paseo) mentioned in note[0].

dar-verb-7cb7de0d.fix: Irregular verb: 'doy' in the first-person singular present, and 'di, diste, dio...' in the preterite.
dar-verb-7cb7de0d.why: Learners need to know that 'dar' is irregular in the present and preterite.

debil-adj-3af279b9.quote: Se escuchaba una débil luz al fondo del pasillo.
debil-adj-3af279b9.fix: Se veía una débil luz al fondo del pasillo.
debil-adj-3af279b9.why: Uses 'se escuchaba' (was heard) instead of 'se veía' (was seen) with 'luz' (light).

debil-adj-3af279b9.quote: Used to describe both physical weakness and weak things like a faint voice or a
debil-adj-3af279b9.why: Merely repeats the two sense definitions without adding new information.

smell-verb-908c9ead.why: Without 'like' or 'of', 'smell' translates simply as 'oler', as in the example.

smell-verb-908c9ead.label: wrong-pos-comparison
smell-verb-908c9ead.fix: Cuando 'smell' describe un olor, va seguido de un adjetivo ('smell good') o de 'like' + sustantivo ('smell like coffee').
smell-verb-908c9ead.why: Contrasts the verb 'smell' with the noun 'scent'; learners need the verb's complement patterns instead.

snake-noun-d1d756ef.quote: En contextos informales, a veces se usa 'serpent' en literatura
snake-noun-d1d756ef.fix: Es el término estándar en la vida diaria; 'serpent' solo se usa en contextos literarios o formales.
snake-noun-d1d756ef.why: Self-contradictory and false: 'serpent' is formal and literary, not informal.

snake-noun-d1d756ef.fix: Animal reptil de cuerpo largo y estrecho, sin patas y cubierto de escamas.
snake-noun-d1d756ef.why: Snakes are covered in scales, not merely 'often' having them.

spring-noun-5b622de6.quote: La palabra 'spring' tiene varios significados muy comunes en inglés
spring-noun-5b622de6.why: Merely restates the three glosses already shown in the entry.

spring-noun-5b622de6.fix: A spring in the old mattress is broken.
spring-noun-5b622de6.why: 'Lost its spring' means lost elasticity (uncountable), not a single metal coil.

spring-noun-5b622de6.fix: Se rompió un muelle del colchón viejo.
spring-noun-5b622de6.why: Mistranslates 'lost its spring' literally; a mattress does not have a single coil.

stomach-noun-e0b3137c.quote: The baby kicked in her stomach.
stomach-noun-e0b3137c.fix: He lay flat on his stomach.
stomach-noun-e0b3137c.why: Unnatural English phrasing and refers to the inside, not the external front of the body.

stomach-noun-e0b3137c.quote: El bebé dio una patada en su vientre.
stomach-noun-e0b3137c.fix: Se tumbó boca abajo sobre el vientre.
stomach-noun-e0b3137c.why: Update translation to match the corrected example for the external body part.

tall-adj-9bc90422.quote: De un objeto que tiene una gran extensión vertical.
tall-adj-9bc90422.why: Having greater than average height for people, trees, or buildings is a single sense.
'Elevado' translates 'high', not 'tall', encouraging the exact confusion warned against in notes[1].

tall-adj-9bc90422.quote: Usa 'tall' para describir personas o cosas que tienen mucha altura vertical.
tall-adj-9bc90422.why: Merely repeats the definitions and uses the pleonasm 'altura vertical'.

rico-adj-44bbcf17.quote: Do not confuse this with 'rico' in a social context, which can sometimes imply
rico-adj-44bbcf17.why: Tells the learner not to confuse the word with itself and adds an unlisted meaning.

tarde-adv-d70fcb11.why: 'In the afternoon' belongs to the noun 'la tarde' and is not in the senses.

tarde-adv-d70fcb11.quote: Used as an adverb meaning 'late', as in 'Llego tarde' (I am arriving late).
tarde-adv-d70fcb11.fix: As an adverb, 'tarde' means 'late'; as a feminine noun ('la tarde'), it means 'afternoon' or 'evening'.
tarde-adv-d70fcb11.why: Only restates the part of speech and gloss instead of distinguishing the noun 'la tarde'.

caro-adj-b40d396d.quote: In some contexts, 'caro' can also mean 'dear' in an emotional sense (e.g., 'el precio
caro-adj-b40d396d.fix: Unlike English 'dear', in everyday Spanish 'caro' only refers to high cost (literal or figurative, as in 'pagar caro' — to pay dearly). For emotional affection, use 'querido'.
caro-adj-b40d396d.why: 'El precio más caro' is figurative cost, not emotional affection; emotional 'caro' is archaic/literary.

la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.why: The feminine noun 'la mañana' only means 'morning', and no sense means 'tomorrow'.

la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.quote: A period of time or an entire day considered in relation to a specific event
la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.why: 'Toda la mañana' is the same sense ('morning') with a modifier, not an entire day.

el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.why: shortGloss includes 'wealth', which is not covered by the senses.

el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.quote: Do not confuse it with change or coins (la moneda), though both relate to payments.
el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.fix: Do not confuse it with 'la moneda' (coin or currency) or 'el cambio' (change).
el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.why: 'La moneda' means coin or currency, whereas change is 'el cambio' or 'el suelto'.

el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.label: example.proper-noun
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.fix: Mi hermano vive en otra ciudad.
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.why: Examples must not contain names of places ('Madrid').

el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.quote: Any male or female person who shares the same parents as another.
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.fix: (in the plural) People who share the same parents; brothers and sisters.
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.why: Singular 'hermano' cannot refer to a female; only the plural 'hermanos' covers mixed-gender siblings.

el-minuto-noun-92bc424a.why: Missing the primary gloss 'minute' (used in the example), and 'second' confuses with 'segundo'.

el-minuto-noun-92bc424a.quote: Used exactly like the English 'minute' for both time and short moments.
el-minuto-noun-92bc424a.why: Restates the senses without adding useful grammatical or usage information.

el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.quote: Note that 'museo' is masculine, so use 'el' or 'un'.
el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.why: Only restates the regular masculine gender already shown in the headword and gender field.

el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.quote: In Spain, you might hear people use the plural 'museos' if they are visiting a
el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.why: Saying a regular noun is used in the plural when there are many is filler.

kupowac-verb-781f5553.quote: Muszę kupować świeże owoce na targowisku.
kupowac-verb-781f5553.fix: Zawsze kupuję świeże owoce na targu.
kupowac-verb-781f5553.why: Imperfective 'kupować' after 'muszę' without a habitual adverb is unnatural; 'targowisko' is overly bureaucratic.

kupowac-verb-781f5553.quote: I need to buy fresh fruit at the market.
kupowac-verb-781f5553.fix: I always buy fresh fruit at the market.
kupowac-verb-781f5553.why: 'I need to buy' requires the perfective 'kupić'; update to match the habitual imperfective example.

kupowac-verb-781f5553.quote: To accept an explanation, story, or excuse as true.
kupowac-verb-781f5553.why: Colloquial calque from English ('to buy a story'), not a core everyday sense for A2.

adj-0eff005c.why: The entry has no sense 'light-colored', and note 1 explicitly contrasts белый with 'light'.

adj-0eff005c.quote: Use белый for things that are literally the color of snow, like paper, milk, or
adj-0eff005c.why: Restates the definition and overlooks common collocations like белый хлеб and белое вино.

adj-0eff005c.quote: Зимой весь город стал белый от снега.
adj-0eff005c.fix: Зимой весь город стал белым от снега.
adj-0eff005c.why: After стал in this construction, Russian naturally uses the instrumental case (белым).

adj-2eb76e52.quote: Use быстрый when talking about speed in movement or action, such as a fast car
adj-2eb76e52.why: Merely restates the definitions of the two senses without adding usage information.

adj-342a5dda.quote: Used to describe people or animals that show kindness and a warm attitude toward others.
adj-342a5dda.why: Restates the definition without adding new grammatical or usage information.

noun-06b6922b.quote: While this word is technically a noun, it functions like an adjective (adjectival noun).
noun-06b6922b.fix: Взрослый is an adjective also used as a noun; it declines like an adjective (feminine взрослая, plural взрослые).
noun-06b6922b.why: It is not 'technically a noun' that functions like an adjective, but a substantivized adjective.

noun-06b6922b.quote: It is the standard, neutral way to refer to someone who is not a child.
noun-06b6922b.why: Restates the definition and the neutral register already shown in the entry fields.

noun-50664da7.quote: Use картина for a painting on a wall or a drawn picture
noun-50664da7.fix: Use картина for a painting, рисунок for a drawing, картинка for a small picture or illustration, and фотография (or фото) for a photograph.
noun-50664da7.why: A drawn picture is рисунок in Russian, not картина, which contradicts sense[0].

noun-63b38367.quote: A container of cloth or plastic you carry things in.
noun-63b38367.fix: A soft container with handles or a strap, made of leather, cloth, or synthetic material, used for carrying things.
noun-63b38367.why: Bags are often leather, whereas a thin plastic carrier bag is пакет, not сумка.

noun-63b38367.fix: Use сумка for a reusable bag, handbag, or sports bag; for a plastic or paper shopping bag, use пакет.
noun-63b38367.why: English speakers commonly misuse сумка for disposable shopping bags (пакет).

noun-83a7e7c6.why: Contains the Polish letter ł instead of a valid IPA symbol.

noun-91420c9c.why: Unstressed 'о' in the first pretonic syllable reduces to [ɐ] in standard Russian.

noun-980d1ea3.quote: Do not confuse this with 'авиация' (aviation), which refers to the industry
noun-980d1ea3.fix: Use 'на самолёте' (in the prepositional case) to say 'by plane': лететь на самолёте.
noun-980d1ea3.why: Learners do not confuse 'самолёт' with 'авиация'; the note only restates the definition.

noun-c32f2ada.quote: In Russian, 'море' refers specifically to the sea. Be careful not to confuse it
noun-c32f2ada.fix: Use 'на море' when talking about going to or vacationing at the seaside (ехать на море, отдыхать на море), and 'в море' for being in the water (купаться в море).
noun-c32f2ada.why: Restates the gloss and warns against an unrelated word ('озеро').

noun-c32f2ada.quote: Metaphorically, 'море' can be used to describe a vast quantity of something
noun-c32f2ada.why: Merely repeats sense 1 without adding usage information beyond what is shown.

noun-d65f1aed.quote: Used for both physical pain and emotional suffering.
noun-d65f1aed.fix: Although 'боль' ends in '-ь', it is feminine (сильная боль). To say something hurts in everyday speech, Russian usually uses the verb 'болеть' (У меня болит голова).
noun-d65f1aed.why: Only summarizes senses 0 and 1 without adding new usage information.

la-primavera-noun-8de86356.quote: Used with the feminine article 'la' or contraction 'en primavera' (in spring) without an article.
la-primavera-noun-8de86356.fix: Usually takes the article 'la' ('La primavera es bonita'), except after 'en' ('en primavera', in spring).
la-primavera-noun-8de86356.why: 'en primavera' is a prepositional phrase, not a contraction.

la-universidad-noun-23f53449.quote: In Spain and Latin America, 'universidad' refers to higher education institutions where you study
la-universidad-noun-23f53449.fix: Do not confuse with 'el colegio', a false friend that means 'school', not 'college'.
la-universidad-noun-23f53449.why: The note only restates the definition without adding usage information.

lleno-adj-066a8598.quote: Use 'lleno' for containers, rooms, or people who have eaten enough.
lleno-adj-066a8598.fix: Usually used with the verb 'estar' ('está lleno') and followed by the preposition 'de' ('lleno de', full of).
lleno-adj-066a8598.why: The note merely summarizes the three senses already given.

no-expression-d81d4edd.fix: Used as a question at the end of a statement to ask for agreement or confirmation. | right, isn't it, don't you
no-expression-d81d4edd.why: Lacks the very common everyday use of '¿no?' as a tag question.

no-expression-d81d4edd.quote: Used as a standard negation to express refusal or disagreement.
no-expression-d81d4edd.why: Restates the definition of sense 0 almost word for word.

no-expression-d81d4edd.quote: Unlike in English, you often use 'no' twice in a sentence:
no-expression-d81d4edd.fix: Spanish uses double negation: 'no' goes before the verb even when another negative word like 'nada' (nothing) or 'nadie' (nobody) follows it, e.g. 'No quiero nada' (I don't want anything).
no-expression-d81d4edd.why: Double negation uses 'no' plus another negative word ('nada'), not 'no' twice.

verb-843f487d.quote: to eat; to drink; to suffer
verb-843f487d.fix: to eat; to take (medicine); to suffer
verb-843f487d.why: Standard Mandarin 吃 does not mean "to drink", and no sense glosses it so.

verb-843f487d.quote: To consume a liquid or take medication.
verb-843f487d.why: Standard Mandarin uses 喝, not 吃, for consuming liquids.

verb-843f487d.quote: Besides food, 吃 is used for drinks that involve a spoon or are considered meals
verb-843f487d.fix: Besides eating food, 吃 is also used for taking medicine, as in 吃药 (take medicine).
verb-843f487d.why: Medicine and noodles are not drinks, and standard Mandarin uses 喝 for liquids.

bakmak-verb-3fe06595.why: The first 'k' in 'bakmak' is voiceless /k/, not voiced /ɡ/.

bakmak-verb-3fe06595.fix: To check, examine, or attend to someone or something. | to check, to examine, to attend to
bakmak-verb-3fe06595.why: Common everyday meaning (e.g. checking a problem, examining a patient, answering the door).

bakmak-verb-3fe06595.quote: Bakmak is a very versatile verb. While its primary meaning is to look,
bakmak-verb-3fe06595.why: Merely restates the definitions and glosses already given in the senses.

bakmak-verb-3fe06595.fix: Bakmak takes the dative case (-(y)e/-(y)a) for the person or thing looked at or cared for (e.g., bana bak, kediye bakmak).
bakmak-verb-3fe06595.why: Learners need to know that 'bakmak' governs the dative case, not the accusative.

uyumak-verb-56fff049.quote: To remain inactive, dormant, or unresponsive.
uyumak-verb-56fff049.why: A2 learners only need the primary sense 'to sleep'; this figurative sense is marginal.

uyumak-verb-56fff049.quote: Proje üzerinde çalışanlar biraz uyudu ama şimdi tekrar hızlandılar.
uyumak-verb-56fff049.why: Unnatural Turkish; applied to people, figurative 'uyumak' means being oblivious, not working slowly.

uyumak-verb-56fff049.quote: Uyumak is the standard verb for sleeping, but it can also describe mechanisms or systems
uyumak-verb-56fff049.why: Restates the glosses and falsely claims the verb Commonly describes inactive mechanisms or systems.

noun-f29d6dec.quote: In Russian culture, the uzhin is typically the main meal of the day
noun-f29d6dec.fix: In Russian culture, 'ужин' is the evening meal, while 'обед' (midday meal) is traditionally the main meal of the day.
noun-f29d6dec.why: Traditionally 'обед' is the main meal in Russian culture; 'ужин' is simply the evening meal.

verb-0851f175.quote: to take; to catch; to rent
verb-0851f175.fix: to take; to pick up; to rent
verb-0851f175.why: The meaning 'to catch' is not present in any of the entry's senses.

verb-0851f175.fix: 'Брать' has an irregular present tense stem with an inserted Vowel: я беру́, ты берёшь, они беру́т.
verb-0851f175.why: Beginners need the irregular present stem 'бер-', which cannot be guessed from 'брать'.

verb-0851f175.fix: Он всегда берёт книги со стола.
verb-0851f175.why: Uses the perfective verb 'взять' ('взял') instead of a form of the headword 'брать'.

verb-0851f175.quote: Мы решили взять машину напрокат на выходные.
verb-0851f175.fix: Мы часто берём машину напрокат на выходные.
verb-0851f175.why: Uses the perfective verb 'взять' instead of a form of the headword 'брать'.

verb-62298af6.quote: This verb describes carrying something by holding it or wearing it as you move somewhere.
verb-62298af6.fix: 'Нести' is a unidirectional verb of motion (carrying in one direction right now). Its multidirectional partner 'носить' is used for repeated trips or wearing clothes.
verb-62298af6.why: 'Нести' never means 'wearing' (that is 'носить'), and the rest just repeats the definition.

verb-ac9e5c2f.quote: Followed immediately by the instrumental case (in Russian, nouns take the ending -е or -ой).
verb-ac9e5c2f.fix: Followed by the preposition 'в' and the prepositional case (в ком/чём). Example: нуждаться в помощи (to need help).
verb-ac9e5c2f.why: 'Нуждаться' governs the preposition 'в' plus the prepositional case, not the instrumental case.
